# graphvec

The graphvec package extends vectors to include graph relationships
between their elements, and offers tools to compute useful summaries of
the graph structure for use in summarising, filtering, and otherwise
manipulating the graph.

Nodes are identified by **position**, not by value: each element of the
vector is its own node, and repeated values are distinct nodes that
happen to share a label. Edges are stored as indices into the vector, so
`graphvec` can represent multigraphs, self-loops and isolated nodes
without any special handling.

## Installation

You can install the development version of graphvec from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mitchelloharawild/graphvec")
```

## Examples

``` r

library(graphvec)
```

### Nodes

A
[`node_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/node_vec.md)
defines a more general graph structure where nodes can have multiple
parents and children.

``` r

nodes <- node_vec(
  x = factor(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "D", "E")),
  from = c(1L, 3L),
  to = c(2L, 5L)
)

nodes
#> <node_vec[6]>
#> [1] A B C D D E
```

This vector describes a graph of six nodes. The two `D` elements at
positions 4 and 5 are *different* nodes, since node identity comes from
position rather than value, and only position 5 is connected to
anything. The `E` element at position 6 appears in no edge at all, and
remains in the graph as an isolated node.

A `node_vec` wraps its values directly, so it keeps behaving like
whatever it wraps. This one is backed by a factor, and still has levels:

``` r

levels(nodes)
#> [1] "A" "B" "C" "D" "E"
```

Subsetting a `node_vec` selects an induced subgraph: edges that lose an
endpoint are dropped, and the surviving edges are remapped to the new
positions.

``` r

nodes[c(2, 3, 5)]
#> <node_vec[3]>
#> [1] B C D
```

These vectors are particularly useful when used in rectangular tidy data
structures, and slice the same way under dplyr verbs.

``` r

tbl <- dplyr::tibble(nodes, id = 1:6)
dplyr::filter(tbl, id %in% c(2, 3, 5))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   nodes    id
#>   <fct> <int>
#> 1 B         2
#> 2 C         3
#> 3 D         5
```

Since node identity is positional, combining two graphs is just a
disjoint union: node vectors concatenate, and the second graph’s edges
shift so they keep pointing at the right nodes.

``` r

g1 <- node_vec(x = c("A", "B"), from = 1L, to = 2L)
g2 <- node_vec(x = c("X", "Y"), from = 1L, to = 2L)

c(g1, g2)
#> <node_vec[4]>
#> [1] A B X Y
```

A special case of
[`node_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/node_vec.md)
is
[`agg_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/agg_vec.md),
which simply identifies a singular parent node in a given vector with
`<aggregated>`. This is a common scenario in data analysis, where a
given dimension is aggregated over.

``` r

agg_vec(
  x = c(NA, "A", "B"),
  aggregated = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)
)
#> <agg_vec[3]>
#> [1] <aggregated> A            B
```

### Edges

The transpose of a node vector is an
[`edge_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/edge_vec.md),
which is instead vectorised along the edges of the graph.

``` r

e <- edge_vec(
  from = c(1L, 2L, 1L, 3L),
  to = c(2L, 3L, 3L, 1L),
  nodes = dplyr::tibble(
    id = 1:3,
    label = c("A", "B", "C")
  )
)

e
#> <edge_vec[4]>
#> [1] [1:A]->[2:B] [2:B]->[3:C] [1:A]->[3:C] [3:C]->[1:A]
```

Values from nodes can be obtained from an edge vector using `$`.

``` r

e$from$label
#> [1] "A" "B" "A" "C"
e$to$label
#> [1] "B" "C" "C" "A"
```

### igraph

Both
[`node_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/node_vec.md)
and
[`edge_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/edge_vec.md)
can be converted to igraph objects for further analysis. The vertex
count is taken from the nodes rather than inferred from the edges, so
isolated nodes are preserved. Direct vectorised statistics and
operations on these vectors are planned for this package in future
releases.

``` r

igraph::as.igraph(nodes)
#> IGRAPH 77387e4 D--- 6 2 -- 
#> + edges from 77387e4:
#> [1] 1->2 3->5
igraph::as.igraph(e)
#> IGRAPH 812a769 D--- 3 4 -- 
#> + edges from 812a769:
#> [1] 1->2 2->3 1->3 3->1
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`agg_df()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/agg_df.md)
  : Create an aggregation table
- [`agg_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/agg_vec.md)
  : Create an aggregation vector
- [`as.igraph(`*`<agg_vec>`*`)`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/as.igraph.md)
  [`as.igraph(`*`<node_vec>`*`)`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/as.igraph.md)
  [`as.igraph(`*`<edge_vec>`*`)`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/as.igraph.md)
  : Convert a graph vector to an igraph object
- [`edge_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/edge_vec.md)
  : Graph vector along edges
- [`graphvec`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/graphvec-package.md)
  [`graphvec-package`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/graphvec-package.md)
  : graphvec: Vectorised graph data structures
- [`is_aggregated()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/is_aggregated.md)
  : Is the element an aggregation of smaller data
- [`new_edge_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/new_edge_vec.md)
  : Constructor function for edge_vec
- [`new_node_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/new_node_vec.md)
  : Constructor function for node_vec
- [`node_vec()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/node_vec.md)
  : Graph vector along nodes
- [`nodes()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/reorient.md)
  [`edges()`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/reorient.md)
  : Reorient a graph vector
- [`` `[`( ``*`<edge_vec>`*`)`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/sub-.edge_vec.md)
  : Subset an edge_vec
- [`` `[`( ``*`<node_vec>`*`)`](https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/graphvec/reference/sub-.node_vec.md)
  : Subset a node_vec
